transcript:
HEADER: Date: 2026-12-09 10:30am PST | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Wu (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood Solutions Eng); Michael Torres (NovaThera - Procurement), Anika Rao (NovaThera - Infosec), David Kim (NovaThera - Legal Ops), Ravi Patel (NovaThera - Cloud Architect)

SUMMARY (auto-generated, may be incomplete): Quick procurement/legal gating sync focused on MSA/DPA redlines, conditional pricing approval, KMS/egress exceptions for clinical test data, and a short technical preflight to validate private deployment perf. Agreed actions include Redwood to send consolidated redline summary, SE benchmark, and customer to provide list of sensitive flows.

TOPICS: MSA redlines; DPA scoping for PHI/CHD; SLA windows and uptime targets; KMS/HSM and key custody options; egress/data residency; conditional pricing (tiered commit + escrow); private vs dedicated tradeoffs

TRANSCRIPT:
00:00 Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, I can see folks dialing in, we'll give it one more minute. Um Maya from Redwood, AE, and with me is Ethan, our SE, and Priya for legal handoffs.
00:18 Michael Torres: good morning, thanks. we just want to make sure procurement can get to a yes this week if possible, we've got the exec siding up on timing, so this is more about the final blockers.
00:32 Maya Patel: yeah understood. quick agenda, align on MSA/DPA redlines, call out any KMS/egress exceptions, confirm SLA ask and pricing condition that finance needs for approval.
00:45 Anika Rao: hi, i'm Anika. from infosec. main thing for us is encryption key control and audit logs for any CHD datasets. we have to know whether keys are customer-managed or redwood-managed and what the escrowing model looks like.
01:02 Ethan Wu: sure. to be clear, Redwood supports both customer-managed KMS within Redwood Private VPC deployments and a BYOK option for Dedicated with HSM supported through partner integration. There's also a key-unwrap flow we can demo.
01:18 Ravi Patel: small clarification, is that available for on-prem? some of our labs are air gapped, so we need an on-prem package or dedicated with no egress. we can't send raw test artifacts out.
01:34 Priya Singh: right, we have an on-prem distribution that can run behind your firewall, that package does not call back to hosted control plane for inference. It's a slightly different SLA and we typically add an operations runbook.
01:49 David Kim: from legal — on the DPA side, the standard redline is around deletion timelines and subprocessor lists. we've got a list of subprocessors that we need to see and a standard 30/90 day deletion window. We may ask for a 0-30 for CHD.
02:08 Maya Patel: ok noted. On the MSA we got your redlines yesterday, we'll produce a consolidated redline document. we'll flag the CHD deletion window and propose a carveout for a 30-day retention for legal hold, and show an escalation path.
02:23 Michael Torres: procurement's practical ask is pricing. we have a conditional approval process — finance will sign off if there's a committed tier with escrow clauses and a performance benchmark that meets our latency tail targets. can we do that?
02:40 Ethan Wu: yes, we can run a dedicated bench — three hour soak against a near-prod trace, measure p95 latency and token cost. we will run both Dedicated and Private builds if you want, but note that private (on-prem) numbers usually show higher latency due to network and hardware differences.
02:58 Anika Rao: also we need to understand what fallback policies look like. if dedicated capacity goes down, what happens to traffic? do we failover to hosted and is that allowed for CHD data?
03:12 Maya Patel: great callout. We generally have a policy that fallback to Hosted API is off for CHD unless the customer opts-in. For Dedicated we can configure automatic fallback to a compatible regional Dedicated pool, otherwise manual failover per the MSA.
03:30 David Kim: we also want to confirm audit logs — token-level tracing for requests, per-route logs retained for at least 180 days for our compliance team. is that possible?
03:46 Priya Singh: yes, Redwood Console can export token-level logs to customer S3 with lifecycle rules — longer retention has cost implications, but it's supported. we'll outline storage pricing separately.
04:01 Ravi Patel: about egress — we have an outbound restrictions matrix. will Redwood honor strict IP allowlists and not use third-party CDNs? we need explicit egress endpoints for firewall rules.
04:16 Ethan Wu: yes, we provide a static egress range for Dedicated and Private; the on-prem package doesn't egress. We'll share the IP ranges and a connectivity checklist in the playbook link.
04:28 Maya Patel: I'll call out that in the MSA we can add the egress clause and the static IP ranges, and we'll attach the network checklist to the onboarding pack.
04:40 Michael Torres: pricing — finance needs a model that shows committed monthly spend, unit token price, and an "escape clause" that if performance degrades beyond xxx p95, they get credits or can step down. Also escrow for pricing if vendor is acquired.
04:58 Maya Patel: we can propose a 12-month commitment with a bilateral escrow clause for pricing for M&A scenarios. We'll draft credit calculations tied to latency SLO breaches — typical is a percentage credit per hour of SLA miss, we'll put sample numbers.
05:15 Anika Rao: on keys — we need the option for Azure/GCP/AWS KMS and also an HSM route. Is Redwood facilitating key wrapping only or do you manage lifecycle?
05:28 Priya Singh: we support KMS integrations and HSM via partner. For BYOK the customer retains key control; Redwood holds wrapped keys. We can document key rotation and access policies in the security packet.
05:43 David Kim: on subprocessors list — we need to see the data processors and whether Redwood uses any third-party telemetry providers for performance metrics.
05:52 Ethan Wu: we'll include a full subprocessor list; for metrics we use in-house telemetry and, optionally, a managed partner for logging — we'll mark that and offer opt-out in the DPA.
06:06 Michael Torres: procurement also wants a short runbook for breach notification timelines and an SLA for incident response (we prefer 1 hour P1 response, with 4-hour remediation target). is that within the MSA negotiation scope?
06:21 Maya Patel: yes that's scope. We'll propose P1/P2/P3 definitions and response windows; enterprise SLA templates usually show 1 hour P1 ack and a targeted remediation SLO, we can attach a draft.
06:36 Ravi Patel: on the technical side — for the benchmark, what's the guidance for the test harness? do you need us to provide a representative 100k token/day trace or can Redwood run synthetic loads?
06:49 Ethan Wu: best is a near-prod trace; if you can't share real traces we can run a synthetic trace that approximates distribution. We'll need sequence length percentiles and payload sizes. We'll also show KV cache impact.
07:05 Anika Rao: clarify on dataflows — we have CHD that must not be persisted outside designated buckets. can Redwood guarantee no caching beyond session if configured?
07:18 Priya Singh: yes, we have config flags for prefix caching and a no-cache mode. For CHD we recommend no-cache and strict per-request token purge. we'll describe this in the runbook.
07:32 David Kim: any limitation for subpoenas or law enforcement — jurisdictional exposure concerns us. how does Redwood handle legal process requests?
07:42 Maya Patel: for hosted customers we comply with lawful process per jurisdiction; for Private/on-prem deployments, the customer controls the environment and Redwood is a software vendor. We'll include language in the DPA/MSA about notification and cooperation.
07:58 Michael Torres: ok practical asks - so timeline: we need redline summary by Friday, benchmark results by next Tuesday, and then an exec sign-off meeting on the 20th. are those dates realistic?
08:12 Maya Patel: yes we can hit that. I'll circulate the redline summary by EOD Friday 2026-12-13 and Ethan will run the benchmark over the weekend and share a spreadsheet and a short writeup by 2026-12-15.
08:26 Anika Rao: one more item — data residency: some datasets must remain in eu-west-1 region. can we lock region for storage and inference?
08:36 Ethan Wu: yes, region pinning is supported on Dedicated and Redwood Private in our EU region. For hosted we have a regional tenancy but you'll need a contractual clause to assert residency.
08:50 David Kim: about pricing approval, procurement may require a three-way signature: procurement, legal, and the business owner — we will confirm the approvers list once we get the redline.
09:02 Maya Patel: perfect. i'll also attach the sample escrow language and the SLA credit table. we'll propose a default credit of 5% monthly for significant SLO breaches but that's negotiable.
09:19 Michael Torres: Thanks. Anything else? i want to note a small risk — if the private package requires hardware procurement, that extends timeline by 6-8 weeks.
09:30 Priya Singh: good point. we'll flag that as risk and propose a hybrid where you start on Dedicated and transition to Private once hardware is procured — we can coordinate a phased migration plan.
09:46 Maya Patel: recap of next steps: (1) Redwood — redline summary + sample escrow + SLA table (Maya) due 2026-12-13, (2) Redwood SE — benchmark and spreadsheet (Ethan) due 2026-12-15, (3) NovaThera — provide sensitive flow list and approvers (Anika/Michael/David) due 2026-12-14, (4) schedule exec review 2026-12-20.
10:10 David Kim: sounds good. we'll review internally and circle back.
10:16 Michael Torres: thanks everyone.
10:18 Maya Patel: thanks team — i'll follow up on the calendar invite and upload docs to the shared drive. link: https://redwood.app/onboarding-playbook (shared doc will include IP allowlist and connectivity playbook). end.
